subject: collecting more iterations with a Stanfit object

messages.author: df68b420342966fc
messages.subject: collecting more iterations with a Stanfit object
parts:
Hi,

Really enjoying RStan, and have a general question about collecting more samples for a pre-existing stanfit object (RStan 2.2.0). The Stanfit object has Rhat values between 1.0 and 1.1, but it looks like the n_effs are a bit low (<100) for some parameters and the CODA raftery diagnostic also suggested more samples would be needed. So basically I just want to collect a few more samples, but using the same model and the same chains (picking up right where the stanfit object had left off and just collecting a few more iterations).

I tried to do this with the code below adapted from the rstan website (https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started#prerequisites).

Newfit <- stan(fit = oldfit, data=data, iter=4500, chains =3)

The first couple of times I tried to run it I got the warning Informational Messages (but over and over again until it crashed). I thought those only applied to convergence and the model had already converged, so I'm a bit confused why those would occur. On one attempt I did get it to run but:

1. The n_effs went down (many to 2!)
2. The Rhat values went up (to values like 13)
3. I now have 2 separate fit objects (although eventually I would like to combine all of my samples)

Does this mean that with more iterations the model is less convergent? Is there a better way of doing this? I also looked for information in the Stan User's Guide, but didn't find anything about this (maybe I missed it?).

I am running R 2.2.0

Thank you for all of your help.

Adrienne

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] collecting more iterations with a Stanfit object
parts:
I'm not sure if RStan has a way of restarting, because it
requires reinitializing with the adapted mass matrices (step scales
and optionally rotation) and time intervals (step sizes). You can
re-use the fit object in RStan to avoid recompiling.

Otherwise, we recommend just fitting more chains and running the
whole thing longer, including warmup, the second time around. We
decided this would be a reasonable strategy because it's going to
take on the order of twice as long to run twice as many iterations.
That's a total budget of 3 time units (1 initial, 2 followup) as
opposed to running from where you left off, which is (1 initial, 1 followup).

And we definitely recommend running in parallel if you have the cores
available.

We're going to add the restart feature relatively soon --- it's one
our high priority list of features for the interfaces.

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] collecting more iterations with a Stanfit object
parts: On Tue, Mar 25, 2014 at 2:32 PM, Adrienne Tucker <atuck...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks Bob, looking forward to another nice feature! In the meantime, would it be possible to obtain an equivalent result by indeed starting over from scratch and running the whole thing longer but recreating the same init values and the same seed values?

If you set the init values and the seeds, you will get the same samples as long as the number of warmup samples is fixed. Just to be concrete about it, if you start with number of warmup samples = 1000 and number of samples = 1000, if you set the number of warmup samples = 1000 and number of samples = 10k, the first 1000 samples will be identical. (If you find that is not true, please let us know and we'll track down the bug.)

With that said, if you went from number of warmup samples = 1000 and number of samples = 1000 to number of warmup samples = 2000 and number of samples = 2000, there's no reason to believe that any of the 2000 samples will be identical to the 1000 samples. Hopefully the inference about the parameters stay the same, but if the model hasn't converged with 1000 samples, you might see different results with 10k samples.





Daniel

Adrienne
